linked_urls.title: Why medicine is creating exciting new frontiers for machine learning // van der Schaar Lab
linked_urls.summary: Medicine stands apart from other areas where machine learning can be applied. Where we have seen advances in other fields driven by lots of data, it is the complexity of medicine, not the volume of data, that makes the challenge so hard. But at the same time this makes medicine the most exciting area for anyone who is really interested in exploring the boundaries of machine learning, since we are given real-world problems to formalize and solve.

linked_urls.title: Why medicine is creating exciting new frontiers for machine learning // van der Schaar Lab
linked_urls.summary: Medicine stands apart from other areas where machine learning can be applied. Where we have seen advances in other fields driven by lots of data, it is the complexity of medicine, not the volume of data, that makes the challenge so hard. But at the same time this makes medicine the most exciting area for anyone who is really interested in exploring the boundaries of machine learning, since we are given real-world problems to formalize and solve.

linked_urls.summary: NOTE: The Call for Socials will remain open. Late Applications will be considered on a case-by-case basis. ICLR 2021 will continue to support the strong community-building role that is so central to the conference. We hope to create opportunities for all participants to meet new people and to share knowledge, best-practices, opportunities, and interests. To enable this, we will support several virtual halls and socials. A virtual hall or social is a participant-led video-driven meeting centred around different themes. These themes can be anything ranging from a gathering around research topics and interests (e.g., generative models, reinforcement learning, covid-19, social impact ML), around skills exchange and training (e.g., giving better presentations, guidance on academic job applications), supporting affinity group meetings (e.g., QueerInAI, Women in Machine Learning), or other social and intellectual gatherings (e.g., 1st virtual conference, ICLR book club). If you are interested in hosting a virtual hall/social, please complete this form. Submit this form before 29 March (anywhere on earth). Notifications of acceptance will go out on 9 April. Virtual halls are typically 2-hour long sessions, must have at least two leads (who will organise the session, moderate the session, and ensure respectful communication). Organisers and guests should be registered participants of ICLR. We will review these as quickly as we can after the deadline. We may combine activities, or suggest other modifications (such as suggesting alternative dates/times) in order to balance the programme of activities. Privacy notice: We collect email addresses to contact you afterwards for feedback about your session. This data can be seen by the ICLR organising committees and their support teams, and identifiable information (e.g., names and emails) will be removed within 6 months of the conference ending.

linked_urls.title: ICLR 2024 Financial Assistance Application
linked_urls.summary: This form is the application point for financial assistance to attend ICLR 2024. This process is managed by the ICLR 2024 DEI Chairs. To fill out this form, you will need: An ICLR.cc account. An OpenReview.net account. If you are planning to attend in person, details of your intended travel to Vienna (including dates, your point of origin, and the approximate cost of travel). A short justification statement for your need for financial assistance. A final decision on any conference, workshop (*), tiny paper, or blog post submissions made to ICLR this year. A short motivation statement on the impact of attending ICLR 2024 on your research career. (*) If you have not heard back from an ICLR 2024 workshop about a submission by the end of March 5th, you can still note your workshop submission in this form. We will be able to take into account workshop papers in our decision process if the workshop announces decisions by March 10th (i.e., they are posted publicly on OpenReview with authors identified); the ICLR Workshop Chairs have communicated this deadline to workshop organizers. With the above info in hand, filling out this form should take 20–30 minutes. Dates: Financial assistance application deadline: March 5th, '24 (Anywhere on Earth) Financial assistance decision notification: March 13th, '24 (Anywhere on Earth) Conference/workshops early registration deadline: March 15th, '24 Eligibility: The ICLR 2024 Financial Assistance program aims to fund student and other early-career contributors to the ICLR conference and workshops. We aim to also consider other inclusion criteria, such as affinity group membership, financial hardship and cost of attendance, and first-time attendance. Financial assistance format: Financial assistance awardees will receive some combination (†) of a complimentary registration (to conference and workshop events) (◊), a complimentary hotel stay between (from 1 to 6 nights, depending on eligibility category) next to the event venue, and/or monetary reimbursement for other expenses (e.g., transit/travel/accommodation). (†) Our default award is complimentary hotel and/or complimentary registration. Reimbursement will be reserved for exceptional cases, such as the need to demonstrate booked travel for a visa application earlier than the financial assistance notification date. The thing I feel most privileged about is the amazing people I had the opportunity to work and talk with from day one of my ML journey.
This also includes my first ML mentor and collaborator Hartmut Neven, who should have been on the paper as he encouraged this line of research and suggested experiments.
Without Hartmut, I would not have had the opportunity to start working on machine learning. In fact, two of us planned to write a paper on adversarial examples in 2012. I am very sad that he was underservedly omitted from the author's list. We considered mending this around 2016, but it seemed too complicated/awkward at that time.
Hartmut is a fantastic person to work with: he was supportive and caring and was very fun to work with. His being left out is my biggest regret about this paper.

linked_urls.title: ICLR 2026 Call for Socials
linked_urls.summary: ICLR supports the strong community-building role that is so central to the conference. We hope to create opportunities for all participants to meet new people and to share knowledge, best-practices, opportunities, and interests. A Social is a participant-led meeting centered around different themes. These themes can be anything ranging from a gathering around research topics and interests (e.g., generative models, reinforcement learning, social impact ML), around skills exchange and training (e.g., giving better presentations, guidance on academic job applications), supporting affinity group meetings (e.g., Women in Machine Learning), or other social and intellectual gatherings. If you are interested in hosting a Social, please complete this form. Submit this form before March 17th AoE. Notifications of acceptance will go out on March 27th AoE. Socials are typically 1.5 - hour long sessions, must have at least two leads (who will organize the session, moderate the session, and ensure respectful communication). Organizers and guests should be registered participants of ICLR. We will review these as quickly as we can after the deadline. We may combine activities, or suggest other modifications (such as suggesting alternative dates/times) in order to balance the program of activities. Privacy notice: We collect email addresses to contact you afterwards for feedback about your session. This data can be seen by the ICLR organizing committees and their support teams, and identifiable information (e.g., names and emails) will be removed within 6 months of the conference ending.
